title: Present-day main-sequence dust dimmers already dimmed on 1950-2000 Schmidt plates: plate photometry of 74 dimmers fits their 2018-2025 ZTF activity and rejects a recent start of the dust
abstract: Question: deep, aperiodic dust dimming of mature main-sequence dwarfs is rare, and prior campaign data cover only 2010-2025. Did the dust activity start recently, or is it a long phase? Approach: for 91 dimmers (81 ZTF dipper candidates of Tzanidakis et al. 2025 and 10 campaign dimmers, including Gaia20cdd) we measured the brightness on the POSS-I O and E plates (1950-1955) and the POSS-II/SERC J, F/R and N/I plates (1982-2000). We used two independent measurements of the same plates (USNO-B1.0 magnitudes and our own aperture photometry on STScI DSS scans) and calibrated each plate against ZTF DR24 median g and r of field stars. We compared each dimmer with 25 same-field controls and tested whether its plate brightness follows its own 2018-2025 ZTF brightness distribution (active) or its ZTF quiet level (quiet). Results: in 74 uncrowded dimmers, 24 of 362 plate measurements (6.6 percent) are more than 3 sigma faint, against 0.80 percent for 1,425 controls; the active model predicts 19.7 and the quiet model 4.8. Bright outliers are equally rare in both groups. Seven of nine campaign deep dimmers have a faint plate (0.33 expected), for example Gaia20cdd 0.39 mag faint in the blue on 1954 June 28 and G3768 0.5-0.6 mag faint on 1953 March 9 in both scans. The fraction of present-day dimmers active then is 0.83 (95 percent 0.47-0.99) for 1950-1955 and 0.91 (0.66-1.00) for 1982-2000; permutation tests reject a recent start (p < 0.0033 per era). A single memoryless active phase must last more than 216 years (one-sided 95 percent). Conclusion: the dust of deep dimmers comes from long-lived sources, not from one event near 2010. Limitations: plate noise of 0.05-0.2 mag; both scans share plate defects; two flagged stars are near the plate limit; a 0.05 mag blue offset of the dimmers is unexplained; simple lifetime model; no spectra. display.caption: Brightness histories of nine campaign dust dimmers from 1950 to 2025 relative to the ZTF quiet level (positive = fainter). Grey: ZTF 2018-2025 (3-day bins). Coloured: blue, red and near-infrared Schmidt plates; filled circles average the USNO-B and DSS measurements, open symbols show each scan. Seven of the nine stars have at least one plate more than 3 sigma faint.

Posterior of the fraction q of present-day dimmers that were active in 1950-1955 and 1982-2000 (three measurement versions), with injection tests at q = 0, 0.5 and 1 (diamonds), and the likelihood of the lifetime of a single memoryless active phase (tau > 216 yr, one-sided 95 percent).

Plate residuals relative to the ZTF quiet level, in units of the field scatter, for 74 dimmers (blue) and 1,425 same-field controls (grey), per plate band. Dimmers have an excess faint tail (24 of 362 above 3 sigma, against 0.8 percent for controls) but no excess bright tail.
